findings.summary: tcn.eval far and udalosti still bind a replay by its bytes alone. In the addendum to his answer to Q31, the lead named 'kontrola(sha256=...) bez cesty' as a gap the content binding must close. tcn/eval.py _pecat_prehratia calls pecat.kontrola(sha256=archive_sha256) only. The replay's configuration.json, as safeguard replay --archive writes it, also names the archive's path ('archive'). So a replay of a re-extraction of a sealed session gets not_sealed there, while the same archive is refused by its content once its path is given. SEALED_RULE and GUARD_RULE state this choice, so the code matches its rule. What B7c guaranteed still holds: the bytes binding is unchanged and checked first, the replay guards bind by the path all three ways, and tcn.eval refuses a sealed role of a campaign index outside the final command (_rola_v5). This is the one sha256-only caller that has the path and does not pass it.

B12 by code reading. events() appends windows and types together. guest() runs before correlation(). The keys of a unit that a type of the session restarts are judged in the journal pass. A line of that unit outside every window of a type that restarts it gives service_restarted_outside_event:<unit>. An unreadable time, or changed keys without a Started line, gives service_restarted:<unit>. Each (window, unit) counts one tolerance. A session without events is judged as before.

Journal forms. In the 4 long lab-trial journals, UNIT_LINE reads every systemd[1] line that names a REQUIRED_UNITS unit (catalog 79, each other app 10, postgres 12). The only exceptions are 4 'Configuration file ... is marked' lines, which are not restarts. The guest writes '+0000' offsets, and fromisoformat reads them. Not read: job lines that give only the description, and lines not in journalctl's short-iso-precise form ('date time host'). Neither can hide a real restart, because systemd also writes '<unit>.service:' lines at every stop.
